claims.statement: John L. Sullivan, with his manager Al Smith and two or three of his company, spent some time in Tom Allen's saloon on Market Street, where a large crowd gathered to look at him.
claims.excerpt: Some time was spent in Tom Kelly's and Ton Allen’:

claims.statement: In Tom Allen's saloon, Sullivan's party retired to a room and drank champagne, while Sullivan himself drank nothing.
claims.excerpt: In Tom Allen’s place the party, with 1 highly favored few, retired to a room

notes: Allen only hosts the visit; he takes no part in the exhibition. Jim Miles's boast names Allen as a man he could hold his own against, but Allen does nothing in it.
